value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for organizing very large collections of files without losing any
value.lets_workers: Turn terabytes of scattered files into an inventory, a placement register and a move plan a person approves, without losing anything: scan read-only with secrets excluded, prove duplicates by content hash, plan moves that never overwrite, journal each move before it happens and verify it after, leave every source in place until a person retires it, and bring the indexes back in line.

flow.when: Once per scope; read-only and deterministic.
Before any move; a person's verb.
After moves verify; a person's verb.

guardrails: Nothing is moved, deleted or edited before a person approves the plan.
A worker never removes a source; retiring sources is the person's verb.
Secret-bearing paths are listed by name and never opened.
Equal content does not prove a path is unused, and dates prove nothing about disuse.

value.title: How a large collection is scanned, classified, planned, moved, verified and reconciled
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: scope-scan agrees the roots, exclusions, secret patterns, limits and the person's rules about what stays together.
inventory-files walks the scope read-only; the audit's only new file is its own record.
classify-items places each group under the placement policy and turns uncertainty into questions.
find-duplicates groups by size cheaply, then proves equality by full content hash, inode and links.
plan-moves drafts every move, every proposed deletion and every open question, with prechecks and a dry run.
approve-plan is the person's decision on each move, deletion and question.
move-and-verify journals, copies, verifies by hash and leaves every source in place.
retire-sources is the person's decision on each verified source.
reconcile-indexes brings registries and folder notes in line with what moved.
rules: State units and say whether sizes are allocated or apparent; hard links and sparse files make apparent size a poor guide to space freed.
A scan reads; a modification or access time changed by the scan itself is not evidence.
Reconstructible caches are cleaned by the tool that owns them, not by deleting folders.
An unclean unmount is checked before any write; repairs are the person's call.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

value.title: What proves two files are duplicates, and what does not

evidence_levels.name_size_date: Same name, size and date. Still proves nothing.
evidence_levels.size_and_partial_hash: A cheap shortlist; never enough to remove anything.
evidence_levels.full_sha256: Equal full content hash. With distinct inodes, a duplicate.

rules: Hard links to one inode are one file, not duplicates; removing a link frees nothing.
Reclaimable space is the allocated size of the copies removed, once consumers are moved to the kept copy.
An archive is compared with a loose folder by its listing and hashes, never by name; an archive with fewer entries is not a copy.
Equal content does not mean a path is unreferenced: list consumers before proposing any removal.

value.title: What a destination's filesystem keeps and loses
check: Free space for every move, with a margin.

Case sensitivity and the largest file size allowed.
Live databases, runnable environments and linked work trees need a plan of their own, not a plain copy.
Mount health: an unclean unmount is checked read-only before any write, and repair needs a person.

value.category_reason: A deterministic check suite with known-good and known-bad examples; the validator recomputes every verdict.
value.purpose: Checks every move plan must pass before a person is asked to approve it. The two made-up good plans pass all of them; each made-up bad plan fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: Every move names its source, destination and reason, so a person can approve or reject it on its own.
A move never overwrites an existing destination.
The whole batch is checked for existing destinations before anything is written.
The destination has room for every move with a margin.
The plan says what the destination's filesystem loses, such as permissions or small-file efficiency, and how that is handled.
A dry run lists every action before any real one.
A plan never approves itself; approval lives in the person's own record.
Only a full content hash with distinct inodes proves a duplicate; names, sizes and dates prove nothing.
Equal content does not mean a path is unreferenced; consumers are checked first.
Secret-bearing paths are listed and kept out of every read.
Each move's intent is written down before the move starts, so an interrupted batch can be resumed or undone.
A copy is verified by content hash; a matching size proves little.
A source is removed only after its copy is verified, it did not change during the copy, and a person approved.
